Definition: properly, vehemence, i.e. (with or without preposition) vehemently; by implication, wholly, speedily, etc. (often with other words as an intensive or superlative; especially when repeated)
BiblicalUsage: The word means very, exceedingly, and might, and it is used where the measure is the whole heart: love the LORD thy God with all thy heart and with all thy soul and with all thy might. God saw everything He had made, and behold, it was very good, and the psalm says His testimonies are very faithful.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the word is a demand for everything: not some of the heart, but all of it, and all of the soul, and all of the might — because the God who made all things very good deserves nothing less.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
